ch.s: Verses 1–4: “Another book which Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah and for those who will come after him, and keep the law in the last days.”; Verses 5–8: “And I asked one of the holy angels who was with me and said to him: 'What is this shining thing? for it is not a heaven, but…”; Verses 9–12: “Who, since they came into being, longed not after earthly food, but regarded everything as a passing breath, and lived accordingly, and the Lord tried them much, and…”; Verses 13–15: “And they shall be resplendent for times without number; for righteousness is the judgment of God; for to the faithful He will give faithfulness in the habitation of…”. People named: Enoch.
q: Read verses 1–4. What is happening, and what stands out to you most?
In verses 5–8, what do you learn about truth and light?
Read verse 13 slowly. What does it say about God, about people, and about how to live?
What does Enoch’s part in this chapter teach you — as an example to follow or a warning to heed?
Where do you see the theme of sin and repentance in this chapter, and how does it connect to the rest of 1 Enoch?
What is one specific way you can put this chapter into practice this week?
ch.a: Ask God to search your heart, confess what He shows you, and make any right amends.
